en: The Legend of the Elder Sumanatthera Sakacintaniyavagga, Number 9 I was once a young man named Sumanas, A student of the Veda, well-versed in the Three Vedas. I was a teacher of the Vedas, possessing great wisdom; I was honored by many people, and I lived in the city of Benares. Then, having heard of the Buddha’s arrival, I went to the place where the Teacher resided. Having approached the Blessed One, the Fully Enlightened One, I paid homage at his feet and sat down to one side. As I sat there, the Teacher, the Great Sage, Taught me the Dhamma, which leads to peace. Having heard that Dhamma, so profound and excellent, I attained the fruit of Stream-entry right then and there. With a heart full of joy, I took my leave of the Teacher, And returned to my own home in the city of Benares. There, I gave away all my wealth to the needy, And then I went forth into homelessness under the Teaching of the Victor. Having gone forth, I practiced with diligence, And soon I attained the state of an Arhat. I am now free from birth, old age, and death; I have done what was to be done and have laid down the burden. This is the legacy of the Elder Sumanas, Told in brief for the sake of the world. May this merit bring happiness to all beings, And may they all attain the bliss of Nibbāna.
“At that time, I was a garland-maker named Sumana;
I saw the stainless Buddha.”
The recipient of the world’s offerings.
Having taken with both hands the most excellent *sumana* flower,
I offered them to the Buddha,
Sikhin, the Kinsman of the World.
By this offering of flowers,
And through my volition and aspiration,
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
because I offered that flower,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
In the twenty-sixth aeon,
there were four of great renown;
The universal monarchs, endowed with the seven treasures;
the four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Sumana speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Sumanatthera is the ninth.
